decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom was a substantial, publicly announced development investment in a high-end segment, so management will attribute its reduced web visibility in 2019 to slow particle therapy adoption and the delayed release, and will persist with it.

Small volume ionization chambers are core dosimetry products with a long lifecycle in accredited calibration workflows, and the product still had a page of its own in 2019, so there is no reason to withdraw it.
As a second small-field chamber that complements the firm's dosimetry portfolio and its platform integration, it is central to the announced direction and was still actively presented in 2019.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a staple product tied to decades of dosimetry expertise and calibration services, so dropping it would contradict the firm's core identity.
Relative dosimetry chambers pair with the firm's water phantoms and scanning systems, so keeping them sustains the integrated workflow the firm has publicly committed to.
Thimble chambers are long-lived reference instruments embedded in customer QA protocols, and their continuous presentation in 2019 shows the firm's ongoing commitment to them.
